newsitem.title: ITALY: Saddam summit plan thwarted - Iraq vice-president.
newsitem.headline: Saddam summit plan thwarted - Iraq vice-president.

text.p: An Iraqi vice-president arrived in Italy on Sunday to attend the World Food Summit and said President Saddam Hussein had also wanted to come but was prevented by U.N. sanctions.
"Unfortunately the embargo prevented him from using a special flight," Taha Mohieddin Ma'rouf told reporters.
U.N. sanctions imposed since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait in 1991 prevent flights into and out of the country.
Iraqis travelling abroad have to journey by road to Jordan. Ma'rouf, a member of Iraq's revolutionary command council, flew to Italy from Amman on a Royal Jordanian Airlines flight.

Iraq intends to use the World Food Summit, which opens on Wednesday at the headquarters of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), to push forward a stalled oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

"He (Ma'rouf) will meet with heads of states and delegations attending the conference to explain the impact of the unjust embargo and their role in alleviating the suffering of the Iraqi people by ending the shortage of food and medicine," the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.
Baghdad signed a deal with the United Nations in May allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months to buy food and medicine. The agreement has yet to be implemented.

Ma'rouf told reporters the five-day summit, which will pledge to reduce the number of undernourished people in the world to half the current level of 840 million by the year 2015, was hugely important.
"We...will do all we can to ensure the summit has a positive outcome," he said.
